text: According to standard homology-modeling guidelines, below approximately what target-template sequence identity does modeling enter the unreliable 'twilight zone'?
explanation: Below about 30% sequence identity, homology modeling enters the 'twilight zone' where alignment errors make models unreliable, and below 20% identity ('night zone') ab initio/deep-learning structure prediction is preferred instead. Thresholds of 50% and 40% are too conservative since good models are routinely built well below those identities, while 10% is already deep in the night zone, past the twilight-zone boundary.
